explanation: This is safe. Optional chaining short-circuits the whole access when user or user.address is null/undefined, so street(user) returns undefined instead of throwing. A tempting wrong answer reads the chain as a plain `user.address.street` access, but each `?.` level guards the next dereference.
prompt: user or user.address may be null. Does street() ever throw a TypeError?
left_label: Safe — optional chaining guards each level
